angle: one scene where this happens, with one subject in it
subject: The kiln opened after the firing, cut away in section: brick walls and a sprung arch round one bowl on its shelf, a pyrometric cone bent beside it and a tapping rod ringing the bowl through the spy hole.
controls: strike: position — the tapping rod draws back from the rim through the spy hole, 36 px off at 0 to 6 px at 100; a note taps it in.
glaze: position — the glaze line on the bowl's outside creeps down from just under the rim to near the foot, the glazed band hatched above it.
crack: shape — a dunting crack runs across the bowl's front from the rim, lengthening and stepping as crack rises; none at 0.
fire: rotation — the pyrometric cone bends over, from nearly upright (10°) at 0 to flat on its pad (90°) at 100, the potter's own gauge of how hot the firing went.
risks: The kiln is a frame round the subject; brickwork must stay quiet (darkest grey hairlines) so the bowl stays the one bright thing. The bowl is small (~125 px) and the cone smaller (~35 px), so crack's line and the cone need checking at 1:1. Striking a bowl inside a kiln is a stretch of the scene (potters ring fresh pots by hand at unloading).
